prompt:
A real photograph, taken with a good phone camera and looking exactly like a phone photograph, of a quiet two-bed patient room on a hospital ward on a bright weekday morning, taken by a nurse standing at the foot of the bed just inside the door, in a tall vertical picture, everything in sharp focus from the floor in the foreground to the window at the back. Natural colours, soft daylight from the window. The textures of real steel, plastic, cotton, glass, paper and skin, with the true depth and the slight lens perspective of a photograph.

Every object stands on its own, with a little space around it, so that the eye can tell at once where each thing is. The whole room carries no writing, numbers, print, symbol or logo anywhere: the drip bag is a plain clear bag of clear liquid, the wristband is a plain white plastic band, the dispenser on the wall is plain white, the wall clock has a plain white face with only twelve short black tick marks, the walls are plain, and the room looks as it could look in any modern hospital in Europe or America.

THE PATIENT'S BED fills the middle of the picture, its foot end towards us at the bottom of the picture and its head end against the back wall: a modern electric hospital bed with a pale-grey steel frame, a pale beech-wood board at its head and at its foot, on four grey castors. Its head section is raised, so that the patient sits half upright against two white pillows. On the LEFT-HAND side of the bed, as we look at it, a grey split side rail is raised along the mattress; on the RIGHT-HAND side the side rail is folded down below the mattress edge, so that side of the bed is open. A small grey handset for the bed, on a coiled grey cable, hangs over the top of the raised left-hand side rail. A white call button on a long white cable lies on the white duvet on the right of the picture, beside him, within reach of his hand.

THE PATIENT, an old man of about eighty-two with a round, friendly face, thin white hair combed back, bushy white eyebrows and a short white moustache, sits half upright in the bed, covered up to the chest by a white duvet in a plain white cover. He wears a plain pale-blue pyjama top with a collar. A thin clear oxygen tube sits under his nose, loops over both ears and runs down behind the head of the bed. His arm on the left of the picture lies on the duvet: a plain white plastic band is around that wrist, and on the back of that hand a small square white plaster holds a thin clear drip line. His head is turned towards the window, and he looks out at the trees with a grumpy, amused frown, his eyebrows raised, as if he were about to make a joke about the weather.

Under the left-hand side of the bed, hooked onto the grey steel frame below the mattress, hangs a small drainage bag in a plain grey fabric cover, its contents hidden by the cover; the edge of the white duvet hangs down over the side of the bed and half hides it.

THE DRIP STAND stands on the left of the picture, beside the head of the bed: a tall slim steel pole on five small castors, with one plain clear bag of clear liquid hanging from its hook at the top; the thin clear line runs down from the bag to the back of his hand.

THE BEDSIDE CABINET stands on the left of the picture, beside the bed and in front of the drip stand, its top a little lower than the mattress: a small white cabinet with one drawer, on castors. On its top, each thing apart from the others: a clear drinking glass half full of water; a plastic feeding cup with a pale-blue spouted lid and two side handles; a pair of reading glasses lying folded; a small skin-coloured hearing aid lying on a folded white paper tissue; and a small closed white plastic box for dentures, with a pale-blue lid.

THE RIGHT OF THE PICTURE, beside the open right-hand side of the bed:
- a grey four-wheeled rollator walking frame stands on the floor beside the middle of the bed, its two handles towards the bed, its brakes on, its small fabric basket empty;
- a pair of dark-blue felt slippers stands side by side on the floor beside the bed, between the rollator and the foot of the bed;
- further forward, near the right edge of the picture, an empty black folding wheelchair stands against the right-hand wall, turned towards the bed.

THE BACK WALL: to the right of the head of the bed, a tall window with a white frame and a white sill, showing a blue sky and the green crowns of tall trees; the window is closed. To the left of the head of the bed, high on the back wall, a round wall clock with a plain white face and twelve short black tick marks.

THE SECOND BED stands at the far left of the picture, along the left-hand wall, only its foot end and its near side in view: the same kind of hospital bed, empty, freshly made with a smooth white duvet and one white pillow. Between the two beds, behind the drip stand, a folded privacy screen on castors stands half open: three tall panels of pale-green fabric in thin white steel frames.

THE FRONT OF THE PICTURE, by the door: on the right-hand wall, at shoulder height, a plain white hand-disinfectant dispenser with a short steel lever, mounted on the wall above the wheelchair. The floor is pale grey vinyl, the walls are warm white, and the bottom of the picture shows the floor in front of the foot of the bed.

The room is clean, calm and full of morning light: between the objects, the same warm white wall and the same pale grey floor.
